title: Jesus Is Born and Grows Up
overview: This chapter tells of Jesus' humble birth in Bethlehem, the people who recognized him as a baby, and a glimpse of him at twelve.

parts.label: Birth in Bethlehem (vv. 1-7)
parts.note: A Roman order to register, likely for taxes, brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, King David's hometown, where the promised king was expected to be born, though scholars still debate how this census date fits Roman records. With the guest space full (probably a family's spare room rather than an inn), the baby is laid in an animal feeding trough.

parts.label: Angels and shepherds (vv. 8-20)
parts.note: Angels announce the birth to shepherds, ordinary workers out at night, rather than to rulers, calling the baby Savior, Messiah (the king God promised to send) and Lord. Their only proof is a baby in a feeding trough, and they find it just as described, spread the news, and leave Mary quietly thinking it all over.

parts.label: Named and presented (vv. 21-24)
parts.note: As Jewish law required, the boy is circumcised and named on his eighth day, then taken to the temple in Jerusalem, where a firstborn son was dedicated to God and a new mother made an offering to end a set time of ritual cleansing. The two birds were the offering the law allowed for families too poor to afford a lamb.

parts.label: Simeon's blessing and warning (vv. 25-35)
parts.note: An old man promised he would live to see God's chosen king holds the baby and says he can now die in peace, because this child will bring light to non-Jewish nations and honor to Israel. He also warns that many will oppose the child and that Mary will suffer deep pain, which Christians read as pointing to her grief at Jesus' crucifixion.

parts.label: Anna, then home (vv. 36-40)
parts.note: Anna, a very old widow who spent her days praying and fasting in the temple, thanks God and tells others who were longing for Jerusalem's rescue about the child. The family returns to Nazareth, where Jesus grows strong and wise.

parts.label: Twelve in the temple (vv. 41-52)
parts.note: On the yearly trip for Passover, the festival remembering Israel's escape from Egypt, Jesus stays behind, and after three days his worried parents find him questioning the religious teachers. His reply about being in his Father's house hints that he sees God as his Father in a special way, yet his parents do not understand, and he goes home and obeys them.

think: Simeon and Anna spent years waiting for something they hoped would come; what have you waited a long time for, and what kept you waiting?
